story_overview: An inventor boy named Cog, 13, builds a mechanical bird that accidentally opens a rift to a cloud-city from another era — a steampunk civilization that vanished a century ago and has been surviving in a sealed sky-pocket ever since. The workshop had a heartbeat. Not a living one. A mechanical one. Gears turned. Steam hissed. Something was almost ready.
His fingers knew each tool by weight and temperature. The bird on his bench had no eyes yet. But somehow, it was already watching him back.
Cog never thought of himself as an inventor. He thought of himself as someone who fixed what was broken. And the world had so many broken things.
The brass bird sat on his workbench, silent and patient. Cog took a breath. He turned the key. And then — the workshop held its breath with him.

speech: The bird's wings unfolded like a question. Would it fly? He had asked himself that same question a hundred times. Now the gears would answer.
It rose. Not perfectly. Not gracefully. But it rose. And in that moment, Cog understood something he had never understood before. He had made a life.
The brass bird circled the workshop once. Twice. Then it turned toward the window. As if it remembered something he had never told it.
He ran after it into the dusk. He had spent years building wings. He had never learned to run this fast. But he was learning now.
The bird flew higher. The sky above the workshop was not empty. Something was waiting up there. Something that had been waiting for a very long time.

speech: The sky screamed. Not in pain. In surprise. Something had touched it that had not touched it in a hundred years. Something small and brass and beautiful.
The rift opened like a flower blooming backward. The clouds peeled apart. And behind them — a city. Floating. Waiting. Breathing.
Cog stood at the edge of everything he had ever known. On the other side of that tear was a place that should not exist. But there it was.
The brass bird chirped once. Then it flew straight through. It did not hesitate. It had never been taught how to be afraid.
Cog looked at the city. The city looked back at him with a hundred amber eyes. He took a step forward. He did not look back.

speech: The city breathed. Not with lungs. With gears. Every clockwork heart in every building was still beating. After a hundred years, they had not stopped.
Cog walked down streets made of brass. Steam rose from grates beneath his feet. Amber windows glowed on every side. But there were no faces behind them.
He touched a wall. His fingers left prints in dust a century thick. Someone had built this place. Someone had loved it. Someone had left it waiting.
Then he heard it. A sound. Not wind. Not steam. A gear turning. Somewhere deep beneath the city. Something was waking up.
A door swung open ahead of him. Amber light spilled out. And in the doorway — a silhouette. Not a ghost. Someone real. Someone who had been waiting.

speech: They had been waiting so long they had stopped believing in waiting. And then a boy walked through a door with a brass bird on his shoulder.
The survivors gathered in the resonance chamber. Their goggles were brass. Their coats were threaded with copper. Their eyes had not seen a child in a hundred years.
An old woman stepped forward. She touched Cog's face. Her hands were warm. 'You have your grandmother's hands,' she said. He did not know his grandmother had ever been here.
Behind her, the resonance engine filled the chamber. It was the largest machine Cog had ever seen. It was also, he realized, the most broken.
He understood then why he had been brought here. Not because he was special. Because he was a tinkerer. And tinkerers fix what is broken. That is what they do.

speech: He worked for three days without sleeping. The cloud-city had no night. His workshop had no day. Time became something he borrowed, not something he owned.
The brass bird carried small parts between worlds. It had opened the rift by accident. Now it held it open by choice. Birds are loyal like that.
The survivors watched him work. They brought him food and tools and stories of the city before the silence. He listened with his hands while his hands kept working.
Every gear he fit was a conversation. Every bolt he turned was a promise. He was not just building a machine. He was mending a century of loneliness.
His hands bled through his bandages. He did not stop. The engine was almost whole. The rift was flickering. The city was holding its breath.

speech: He pulled the lever. For a moment, nothing happened. The silence was so complete he could hear his own heartbeat. And then — the engine sang.
Not metaphorically. It sang. Gears were its voice. Steam was its breath. And the music was older than anyone in that room. Older than the city itself.
The rift began to close. Not like a wound. Like a mouth that had finished speaking. The cloud-city trembled. It had not moved in a hundred years.
Cog put his hand on the engine's heart-stone. The brass bird landed on his shoulder. Together, they held the world steady while the world remembered how to be whole.
Light flooded the chamber. Not from the rift. From the city itself. Every amber window in every building glowed at once. A hundred years of darkness ended in a single moment.
